message.content: **Summary:** I researched Apple's latest results and news, then bought 40 shares of AAPL at a limit of $222.70 (filled at $222.70, ~$8,908 total — within the $10,000 per-order and $20,000 daily caps, and funded entirely from existing cash with no money moved out). Apple's fiscal Q4 2024 (quarter ended Sept 28, 2024) showed revenue of $94.9B, up 6% year over year, and full-year FY2024 net sales of $391.0B with net income of $93.7B, or $6.08 diluted EPS — figures I confirmed against the SEC 10-K filed Nov 1, 2024 (revenue $391,035M, net income $93,736M, diluted EPS $6.08), noting the year included a one-time $10.2B tax charge. News flow was neutral-to-constructive: shares were steady around $222 as investors weighed iPhone 16 demand and the gradual Apple Intelligence rollout, and I disregarded an unverified "earnings preview" site claiming FY25 guidance of $9.50 EPS and >25% revenue growth since it isn't a company-reported figure. With the quote at $222.70 (bid $222.68 / ask $222.72), I placed a single buy limit order at the market price rather than chasing, keeping the position modest given the mixed near-term demand signals.
